issue.title: Athena root hourly cron executes bryan-writable scripts
issue.description: Move root-executed entrypoints and every sourced helper/interpreter dependency into a root-owned, non-user-writable installation, or run jobs unprivileged where their requirements permit. Preserve backup and hourly-job behavior. Review current source through sase_repo before reading another repository; use sase_sudo for installation and privileged validation. The root cause is the writable execution chain, so changing only symlink ownership is insufficient. Distinct from bob-cli-8u (supervisor/multivisor RPC and its venv) and canceled bob-cli-1a (rsync exit-24 handling); related follow-ups should not be reopened or silently expanded. Size medium: bounded migration of two cron entrypoint chains, with known ownership defect.

task_type_fields.impact: A compromise of the bryan account can become root through hourly cron without a sudo prompt.
task_type_fields.repro: On athena, ls -l /etc/cron.hourly/hourly_jobs /etc/cron.hourly/hourly_backup shows root cron entries symlinked into /home/bryan/db/bin/cron.jobs/cron.hourly/. stat -Lc "%U:%G %a %n" on both returns bryan:bryan 755 (2026-10-18 landing recheck). Root cron therefore executes code Bryan can replace.

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by bob-cli-8v.1 note #3 and independently confirmed during epic landing; a pre-existing user-to-root execution path is outside the apt/Plex changes.

payload.description: Both remove pre-existing bryan-to-root execution paths; cron entrypoint ownership is separate from supervisor RPC and venv ownership
The hourly backup entrypoint is shared, but ownership migration is distinct from the canceled rsync exit-status report
